title: Forms: controlled and uncontrolled
summary: Controlled inputs with value and onChange, uncontrolled inputs with defaultValue and refs or FormData, checkboxes and selects, validation, and the controlled/uncontrolled warning.

sections.title: Controlled inputs
sections.body:
A **controlled** input takes its value from state and reports changes: `<input value={name} onChange={e => setName(e.target.value)} />`. React keeps the DOM in sync with state, so you can validate, format or disable the submit button as the user types.

Checkboxes and radios use `checked` and `e.target.checked`. A `<select>` and a `<textarea>` take `value` too (no `selected` attribute on options, no children text in the textarea). `value` without `onChange` makes a read-only input, and React warns.

sections.title: Uncontrolled inputs
sections.body:
An **uncontrolled** input keeps its own value in the DOM. Give it `defaultValue` (or `defaultChecked`) and read it when you need it: on submit with `new FormData(e.currentTarget)` and `name` attributes, or through a ref. This is less code for simple forms and works well with React 19 form actions.

Do not switch an input between controlled and uncontrolled: `value={user.name}` when `user.name` starts `undefined` triggers "A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled". Start with `""`.

sections.title: Submitting and validating
sections.body:
Handle `onSubmit` on the `<form>`, not `onClick` on the button, so Enter in a field submits too. Call `e.preventDefault()` to stop the page reload. A `<button>` inside a form defaults to `type="submit"`; give other buttons `type="button"`.

Validate on submit (and optionally on blur), show messages next to the field, link them with `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid` on bad fields. Keep errors in state alongside the values, or derive them from the values.

pitfalls: `value` without `onChange` (read-only input) or with an `undefined` initial value (controlled/uncontrolled switch).
Reading `e.target.value` for a checkbox instead of `e.target.checked`.
Handling submit with `onClick` on the button, so Enter does not work, or forgetting `preventDefault`.
Extra buttons inside a form without `type="button"`, which submit the form.

gotchas.question: What does typing into `<input value="hi" />` do?
gotchas.answer: Nothing: the value is fixed at "hi", because it is controlled with no `onChange`. React warns and suggests `defaultValue` or `readOnly`.

gotchas.question: Which is controlled: `<input defaultValue={name} />` or `<input value={name} onChange={…} />`?
gotchas.answer: The second. `defaultValue` only sets the initial DOM value; later changes to `name` do not update the input.
